subject: editGrob on a ggplotGrob returned object

messages.author: 427356d65a15c6cc
messages.subject: editGrob on a ggplotGrob returned object
parts:
Dear all,

in ggplot2 0.9.1, following code would work, but in 0.9.2, the ggplotGrob return a gtable and following code give some errors

> library(ggplot2)
> p <- qplot(wt, mpg, data = mtcars, colour = cyl, main = "title")
> g <- ggplotGrob(p)
> g <- editGrob(g, "title-2-2", gp = gpar(fontface = "italic"),
+                  grep = TRUE, global = TRUE)
Error in editGrob(g, "title-2-2", gp = gpar(fontface = "italic"), grep = TRUE,  : 
  It is only valid to edit a child of a 'gTree'

so what's the equivalent for the code above to edit a specific grob on the fly?

Thanks

Tengfei

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: editGrob on a ggplotGrob returned object
parts:
g is a gtable object. You can inspect it with the following:

# Show the structure of the gtable object, but don't recurse into sub-components
str(g, max.level=1)

# Print the data frame recording layout
g$layout

# Get the list of grobs in the gtable
g$grobs

# Get a 1x1 gtable that contains just the title
g[2,4]



This code will have the effect you're looking for. It might be worth
thinking about how to modify the gtable API to make this sort of
access easier.

library(ggplot2)
library(grid)
library(gtable)
p <- qplot(wt, mpg, data = mtcars, colour = cyl, main = "Title text")
g <- ggplotGrob(p)

# Get index of the title grob
idx <- which(g$layout$name == "title")

# Modify the title grob and save it back
g$grobs[[idx]] <- editGrob(g$grobs[[idx]], gp = gpar(fontface =
"italic", col="red"))

grid.draw(g)



It would also be nice to be able to do something like grid.ls() on a
gtable and get back a useful result.

-Winston
